The passage explains that China’s primary military threat after the mid-1300s came from highly mobile steppe nomads, against which early heavy and slow-firing gunpowder weapons were not effective.  
Therefore, China focused instead on improving horse archer units, which were better suited to countering that threat.  
This matches the idea that they logically developed weapons suited to their immediate military needs rather than pursuing ineffective gunpowder innovations.
